The discarded term is 2 e^a f^b h^(c−2)(Δ−λ). Iteration gives linear remainder and division maps N,Q with f=N(f)+(Δ−λ)Q(f), h-degree of N≤1, total degree of N≤deg f and of Q≤deg f−2. For a Gauss weight ρ>=1, coefficients integral imply ||N||≤1 and ||Q||≤ρ^(−2). These maps extend to weighted-c0 PBW completions; iterating over commuting sl2 factors gives the corresponding multi-central decomposition.
items.locator: Explicit proof completion of Fu §3 central PBW calculation and §5 final topological PBW paragraph; uses the normal-form basis and Frommer weighted-PBW description.
items.note: This addresses the U_r central quotient normal form. It does not prove separation of Fu's weaker filtration on D_r central quotients, nor the all-real-radius domain claim. The polynomial identity and finite degree bounds have exact regressions; Banach extensions remain proposed mathematical proof steps, not formalized declarations.

items.name: Weighted PBW Banach completions for integral sl2 lattices
items.statement: For g_0=sl2(Z_p)^m, odd p and real ρ>=1, complete U(g_0)[1/p] for the norm of a finite ordered-PBW sum sup_α |c_α|ρ^|α|. The carrier consists of PBW coefficient families with |c_α|ρ^|α|→0. Integral structure constants and degree-nonincreasing PBW rewriting give submultiplicativity, so multiplication extends continuously to a Banach algebra B_ρ. For ρ=1 this is the integral p-adic enveloping completion followed by inversion of p.
items.locator: Fu §3 completion and §5 equation(27); explicit reusable weighted-completion interface for the Frommer comparison.

api.name: WeightedPBWCompletion.series
api.statement: A weighted-c0 coefficient family defines the norm limit of its finite ordered PBW sums.

api.name: WeightedPBWCompletion.ext
api.statement: Two completed elements agree iff all coefficients in the fixed ordered PBW basis agree.

api.name: WeightedPBWCompletion.changeRadius
api.statement: For 1<=ρ'<=ρ the coefficient-preserving B_ρ→B_ρ' map is a continuous injective algebra map and these maps compose.

uses.how: Complete the bounded PBW division operators and identify the closed normal-coefficient space.

items.name: Existing restricted power-series subring
items.statement: For a normed ultrametric ring R and real radius c, use the existing subring of R[[T]] defined by ||a_n|| c^n tending to zero. For c>0 this supplies the one-variable commutative coefficient model and its polynomial examples; no analytic-group distribution algebra or Banach completeness theorem is claimed.
items.locator: Pinned Mathlib RingTheory/PowerSeries/Restricted.lean, IsRestricted, isRestricted_iff and IsRestricted.subring.

api.name: RestrictedSeries.coefficients
api.statement: Membership is equivalent to the weighted coefficient sequence tending to zero.

api.name: RestrictedSeries.monomial
api.statement: Every monomial a T^n belongs to the restricted subring.

api.name: RestrictedSeries.mul_mem
api.statement: The product of two restricted series is restricted when the coefficient norm is ultrametric.

uses.how: Calibrate weighted-c0 versus bounded coefficients in the one-variable commutative case; this does not replace the noncommutative convolution construction.

items.name: Existing last maximal weighted coefficient
items.statement: For a nonzero power series over a normed ring, restricted at positive real radius c, some index n attains the Gauss norm and every later weighted coefficient is strictly smaller. No discreteness or completeness hypothesis is required.
items.locator: Tau Ceti RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean, exists_max_eq_gaussNorm_of_isRestricted.

items.name: Existing multiplicativity of the restricted Gauss norm
items.statement: For restricted f,g at c>0 over a normed ring with ultrametric distance and multiplicative norm, ||fg||_c=||f||_c ||g||_c. This is the ordinary one-variable power-series theorem, not a theorem about arbitrary analytic distribution algebras.
items.locator: Tau Ceti RingTheory/PowerSeries/GaussNorm.lean, gaussNorm_mul_of_isRestricted.

items.name: PBW over a commutative ring with a free Lie basis
items.statement: Let R be a commutative ring and L an R-Lie algebra with a chosen totally ordered R-basis. The increasing ordered products of powers of its basis vectors form an R-basis of U_R(L), and the associated graded map Sym_R(L)->gr U_R(L) is an isomorphism taking each basis generator to its degree-one symbol. No characteristic-zero or algebraic-closure hypothesis is imposed.
items.locator: Reusable integral PBW input of Fu §3 and AW13 §10.3; the original general-ring PBW proof remains a source-decomposition task.

items.name: The unramified maximal-ideal filtration
items.statement: Let R be a complete DVR with uniformizer p, p odd, residue field k, G uniform of dimension d, b_i=g_i-1 for an ordered minimal generating set, and m=ker(R[[G]]->k). Then deg_m(sum a_alpha b^alpha)=min_alpha(v_p(a_alpha)+|alpha|), the filtration is complete, and gr_m R[[G]] is U_{k[t]}(gr G tensor_Fp k), with gr G tensor k identified with t(h/ph)[t] for h=p^(-1)R L_G. In particular this graded ring is a noetherian domain.
items.locator: AW13 published §§10.1–10.3, pp.532–535; hypotheses preceding the theorem are essential.

items.name: Strict exponential comparison for microlocalization
items.statement: Under unramified-graded-iwasawa, let A=Uhat(h)[1/p]. The map b_i -> exp(pu_i)-1 extends to a strictly filtered map R[[G]]->A, where u_i is the normalized Lie basis. It sends the symbol of p to an invertible Laurent variable s and the symbol of b_i to s u_i. Thus the induced map from Q_gr(p)(R[[G]]) has bijective associated graded map and is an isomorphism of complete filtered rings.
items.locator: AW13 Theorem10.4 and full proof, pp.535–536.

items.name: Finite coefficient extension of completed group rings
items.statement: For a profinite group G and a finite extension K/Q_p with integers O_K, the canonical O_K tensor_Zp Z_p[[G]] -> O_K[[G]] is an isomorphism of topological O_K-algebras. After inverting p, K tensor_Qp Q_p[[G]] -> K[[G]] is an isomorphism. Tensor products here are ordinary finite coefficient extension, with the transported finite-module topology; do not replace bounded-denominator K[[G]] by lim_U K[G/U].
items.locator: Derived finite-free coefficient comparison for Fu §4; supplier PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L1.

items.name: Finite coefficient extension of PBW completions
items.statement: For K/Q_p finite, g_0=sl2(Z_p)^m and real rho>=1, finite coefficient extension identifies K tensor_Qp B_rho(Q_p) with B_rho(K), where both completions use ordered PBW coefficients with ||c_alpha||rho^|alpha|->0. The map is a topological algebra isomorphism, generally not an isometry for an arbitrary integral basis. For lambda in Z_p^m it commutes with the central quotient by Delta_i-lambda_i.
items.locator: Derived coefficient comparison for Fu §5 and the AW14 alternative proof.

items.name: Ramified coefficient comparison through the base-field microlocal map
items.statement: For odd p and G=ker(SL2(Z_p)->SL2(F_p))^m, extend the Q_p microlocal map to a finite K/Q_p using finite-group-ring-coefficients and finite-pbw-coefficients at rho=1. The resulting map K[[G]] -> Uhat(sl2(O_K)^m)[1/p] is flat and agrees with g -> exp(log g). This gives the coefficient extension required by Fu; it does not identify a ramified maximal-ideal set union_a(p^a+m^(a+1)) with an Ore denominator set.
items.locator: Fu §4 (17)–(18), corrected coefficient interface using AW13 §10.1 and Theorem10.4.

items.name: Closed central ideals with an attained quotient norm
items.statement: Fix odd p, integral lambda in Z_p^m and rho>=1. In B_rho, let I_lambda=sum_i B_rho(Delta_i-lambda_i). The successive bounded PBW remainder N fixes exactly the closed weighted-c0 span of ordered monomials with every h_i-degree at most one, has norm<=1, satisfies N^2=N, and has kernel exactly I_lambda. The quotient norm on B_rho/I_lambda is attained by N(f) and equals ||N(f)||_rho. Thus I_lambda is closed and the quotient is a nonzero Banach algebra.
items.locator: Derived strengthening of Fu §3 Lemma3.3 and §5 topological PBW step; continuation of bounded-central-division.

items.name: Injective radius change after central reduction
items.statement: For odd p, integral lambda and 1<=sigma<=rho, the coefficient-preserving map B_rho/I_lambda -> B_sigma/I_lambda is injective. It takes the normal PBW coefficient family at rho to the same family at sigma. It need not preserve norms when sigma<rho.
items.locator: Derived radius comparison completing Fu §5 final PBW paragraph.

items.name: Domain property for weighted central enveloping quotients
items.statement: For odd p, lambda in Z_p^m and every real rho>=1, B_rho/I_lambda is a nonzero domain. This statement does not assert noetherianity at every real weight.
items.locator: Derived from Fu Lemma3.3 at weight one and the coefficient-preserving radius injection.

items.name: Small real radii: logarithmic and PBW coordinates coincide
items.statement: Let p be odd, G=ker(SL2(Z_p)->SL2(F_p))^m, and p^(-1)<=r<p^(-1/(p-1)) be any real radius. Put rho=pr. The enveloping map e_i,f_i,h_i -> p^(-1)log(1+b_i) extends, in a consistent ordered basis, to an isometric Banach algebra isomorphism B_rho -> D_r(G,Q_p). Its inverse on group coordinates is b_i -> exp(p x_i)-1. No rationality assumption on log_p(r) is required in this small-radius statement.
items.locator: Derived completion of Fu (27),(30); uses convergent logarithm/exponential and the first-congruence Lie comparison.

items.name: Central distribution quotients at all small real radii
items.statement: Under small-radius-log-exp and for integral lambda in Z_p^m, the actual ideal sum_i D_r(Delta_i-lambda_i) is closed and the quotient is a nonzero domain with the attained normal-form quotient norm. This holds for every real p^(-1)<=r<p^(-1/(p-1)). It does not establish Fu5.7 for larger radii or prove injectivity from a larger central distribution quotient.
items.locator: Derived small-radius case of Fu Theorem5.7 with explicit separatedness.
